id: title:adamleithp:markdown lists and code in the composer

review.posthog_relevance: Desktop message editor markdown support and paste handling
review.reason: The change group implements markdown rendering, input rules, and paste parsing for the Desktop message editor. P1.F1 and P1.F2 establish the CSS and Tiptap behavior for lists and code blocks. P1.F7 adds the markdown parser and input rules. P1.F11 and P1.F10 implement and test the markdown paste parsing, while P1.F12 removes redundant implementations. This represents a substantive,
review.uncertainty: The tier is assigned based on the implementation and test coverage of markdown support and paste handling, which could improve the Desktop editor experience. However, the actual benefit to PostHog users and the reliability of the implementation are not independently verified. No tier assignment is performed here; only observations are recorded.

observations.limitations: This chunk is a single, cohesive change group. No unrelated PRs detected. No tier assignment requested.

observations.behavior: Adds CSS rules for markdown rendering, including list and code block styling, to preserve formatting and compatibility with Tailwind and existing editor instances.
observations.posthog_connection: Provides consistent markdown display for the Desktop message editor, including lists and code blocks, without relying on DOM classes that could break compatibility with older editor instances.

observations.behavior: Adds a Tiptap extension to handle Shift+Enter behavior, inserting newlines in code blocks and splitting list items.
observations.posthog_connection: Allows users to insert newlines in code blocks and split list items using Shift+Enter, rather than the default Enter behavior, improving markdown editing experience.

observations.behavior: Adds tests for markdown parsing and bash mode detection, including round-trip serialization and bash mode detection.
observations.posthog_connection: Provides tests for markdown parsing and bash mode detection, including round-trip serialization and bash mode detection, ensuring compatibility with markdown input and bash mode detection.

observations.limitations: This chunk is a single, complete change group. No missing context or unrelated PRs detected. No score assigned; tier requires assessment of PostHog benefit and tier justification.

observations.behavior: Adds a new markdown parser and input rules for the desktop message editor, including markdownDoc.ts, markdownInputRules.ts, and markdownInputRules.test.ts.
observations.posthog_connection: Adds markdown parsing and input rules to the desktop message editor, potentially improving markdown support and input behavior.

observations.limitations: This chunk is a single, cohesive change group. No unrelated PRs are indicated. No tier assignment is performed here; only observations are recorded.

observations.behavior: Adds a new test file P1.F10.H1 with 63 lines of tests for markdown paste parsing, including cases for bullet lists, numbered lists, nested lists, fenced code blocks, inline code, and prose preservation.
observations.posthog_connection: These tests guard the markdown-paste parsing implementation, not the implementation itself. They do not demonstrate the benefit of the change.

observations.behavior: Adds P1.F11.H1, a 56-line implementation of insertPastedMarkdown, which converts pasted markdown into ProseMirror nodes rather than plain text, while preserving prose and avoiding insertion inside code blocks.
observations.posthog_connection: This implementation could prevent users from pasting markdown as plain text, preserving formatting and structure. It could also prevent unintended insertion of markdown into code blocks.

observations.behavior: P1.F12.H1 removes the editorContentToTiptapJson and tiptapJsonToEditorContent implementations from useDraftSync and replaces them with imports from markdownDoc, while retaining the same exported interface and DraftContext.
observations.posthog_connection: This could preserve compatibility with the markdownDoc implementation while removing redundant or potentially buggy implementations.
